Q1: Middle path (도메인 소유자 결정): Include locomotion technologies that directly transfer to humanoid robots — bipedal/legged walking, balance control, whole-body motion control, fall prevention and recovery — even when not exclusively designed for a humanoid platform. EXCLUDE generic wheeled mobile platforms, AGVs, logistics/transport robots, and navigation or fleet control of generic (non-legged, non-humanoid) mobile robots.
Q2: Middle path (도메인 소유자 결정): Include actuators, joints and robot hands used for human-like manipulation — multi-fingered robot hands, dexterous grippers, grasping mechanisms, tactile-sensing hands, and joint/actuator modules (including soft actuators and reducers/servo modules) serving robot arms, hands or legs — even when not exclusively designed for humanoids, because actuators and robot hands are the representative commercialization bottleneck of this domain. EXCLUDE actuators exclusively dedicated to unrelated fields (e.g., implantable medical devices, vehicle powertrains) with no human-like manipulation or humanoid-joint role.
Q3: Middle path (도메인 소유자 결정): Include human-robot safety and physical human-robot interaction technologies — proximity/co-working safety, collision detection and mitigation, compliant/impedance control for safe contact, safe handover — as these transfer directly to humanoid commercialization. EXCLUDE fixed industrial collaborative robot arms as complete systems when they have no humanoid features and their contribution is not a transferable safety/HRI technology.
